entities.summary:
Pahemnetjer (p3-ḥm-nṯr; "servant of the god", "priest") was a High Priest of Ptah during the reign of Ramesses II.






He succeeded Huy as High Priest of Ptah and was in turn succeeded by his son Didia.






Pahemnetjer's role as High Priest of Ptah was crucial in the temple's administration and in the city's religious life during the 13th century BCE.






As High Priest, Pahemnetjer oversaw the construction of temples, the performance of rituals, and the management of the priestly class.






His leadership played a significant role in maintaining the stability and prosperity of Thebes during a time of significant political and economic upheaval in ancient Egypt.






Pahemnetjer's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he contributed to the development of the Egyptian priestly class and the preservation of ancient Egyptian religious traditions.
